decision: read the record layout: 24-byte PAL header (uuid 46539, size 73888, 257, 0, 1080<<16|1920, 0), then ia_pal_isp_nntm_1_0_t at the report's offsets, 4 bytes padding
why: the report's offsets only line up with a 0x18 header; with that every field lands (offsets 0,128,128 at +0x08, flags at +0x5c, map at +0x64, 63x47 at +0x10064, LUT at +0x10080)

decision: compared the constant fields with nntm_control
result: matrices, offsets, a=2 b=512 c=0, guide 27955/-12919 equal; range flags 1,1; map centre 22417 (350/1023) at sequence 0 then 32031 (500/1023); LUT all 0x7fff

decision: checked the pipeline with the extra group
evidence: runs/x1-b (last file 00299.nv12), runs/head-a vs x1-a error lines, dmesg since 63637
result: 300 of 300 frames, same three HAL ERR/WARN lines as branch head, no kernel errors; 11.4 vs 11.3 fps (dim room, 100 ms exposure)

decision: HAL keeps the record per sequence in AiqResultStorage and exports camera_get_nntm_params(camera, sequence, data, size)
why: the HAL owns computing; AiqResultStorage is already per camera and per sequence and reachable from the API without threading through CameraHal, CameraDevice and PipeManager
result: builds; 300 of 300 frames on the scratch build (runs/u1-a)

decision: stored the whole PAL record, header included
why: its uuid and size are the version and size check the element needs, and nothing has to be invented for it

decision: fixed unit 1: camera_get_nntm_params was not reachable, libcamhal.so is an adaptor that dlopens the real HAL; added it to HalAdaptor's table
why: icamerasrc failed to load with undefined symbol camera_get_nntm_params in its install check
evidence: nix log of the failed icamerasrc build, hal-nntm-params.patch HalAdaptor.cpp
result: fixed in this commit, not by rewriting c1c2590

decision: one parameter type NntmParams = what nntm_1_0 hands the stage (flags, offsets, matrices, a b c, guide, blend map with size); constants become nntm_params_samsung(), the record parser nntm_params_from_record(); reference.py mirrors both
why: the kickoff's shape: one type, constants as its fallback value, no second code path
result: check.py passes on cpu (sandbox) and gpu (gpucheck.txt)

decision: metadata = the HAL's PAL record unchanged, as custom meta GstNntmParamsMeta {record: GBytes}; the record's own uuid and size are the version check; a frame without one or with a foreign one gets the constants and one g_warning
why: nothing to invent: the header already identifies the kernel and its size; stderr because the relay drops bus warnings
result: check.py: foreign records give output identical to no records (0 difference)

decision: back ends take parameters per frame (set_params) and keep only size work in configure; the CPU back end interpolates the 63x47 map per pixel instead of upsampling it once
why: the map changes every frame (gain, shading, face ramp); a full-resolution table rebuilt per frame would cost tens of ms on the CPU
result: live: cpu equals reference exactly, gpu within 1

decision: the element keeps Samsung's guide weight and bias even when the record carries others
why: Windows' executor never forwards them (DERIVATION 7); check.py writes zeros there to prove they are ignored
result: matches the Windows behaviour as read

decision: live check through the relay's shape (icamerasrc ! nntm range=limited) with a tap tool that keeps frames 0..19 in memory and writes them after the run
why: frames from the stream start keep the temporal filter state comparable with reference.py; writing at full rate stalls the HAL
result: runs/u2-cpu: 20 frames, max 0, 0 bytes differ; runs/u2-gpu: max 1, 0.64 % of bytes

decision: checked strength against sensor gain with manual gain 0, 3, 6, 12 dB (sensor analogue gain 1.0, 1.375, 1.94, 3.9) and the dim room on auto (15.5x)
why: no bright scene in front of the camera this morning; the manual runs move the real sensor gain the library reads
result: map centre 22417 (350/1023), 26392 (412), 31965 (499), 32029 (500), dim 32029 (500): VERIFIED, natural daylight not seen

decision: compared the received blend map with the one reference.py builds from shading.f32
result: differs: corners relative shading 0.25 against F11's 0.16 at every gain, up to 5 % of the map maximum; the received one is right (the kernel uses the frame's own shading grid, as on Windows); dim room fits radial 500/1023
